title: ATO findings report
description: Output of `ato scan --format json`. Found values are never included; `masked` keeps at most the last few characters.

schema_version.description: 2.2 added the kinds file and record, special_category on value findings, the sink session-replay and criminal-convictions-and-offences (GDPR Art. 10) to special_category; 2.1 added possible on findings; 2.0 renamed the tool from pii-eu to ato (tool.name is ato) and changed no field; 1.3 added not_read on skipped and sampled files; 1.2 added the kinds sink, infra and lifecycle, the store object and sink, data_category and column_name on findings, and sampled and columns in the summary; 1.1 added kind and special_category. Older 1.x reports are 2.0 reports without those fields.

name.description: The command that wrote the file: ato from 2.0, pii-eu before.

ignored.description: Findings left out by an `ato:ignore <reason>` comment (or the deprecated `pii-eu:ignore <reason>`).

baselined.description: Findings left out because they are in the baseline.

sampled.description: Data files of which only the first rows were read (`--max-rows`, `max_rows`). Absent when none were sampled.

columns.description: Findings grouped by file and column, for findings that have a column_name, in order of first appearance. Counts follow the reported findings. Absent when no finding has a column.

kind.description: value: personal data found in text. field: a schema or model field whose name says it holds special-category data (GDPR Art. 9) or criminal data (Art. 10); masked then holds the field name. sink: a log, error-tracker or analytics call that is passed personal data, or session replay set up to record form inputs; masked then holds the expression passed or the setting, never a value. infra: a data store declared in Terraform without encryption, a retention limit or EU residency, or open to the public; masked then holds the resource address. lifecycle: a table or model holding personal data with no erasure path or no retention limit in the code; masked then holds its name. file: a file that holds personal data as a whole or in its metadata (a database dump, a photo with a GPS position, a document naming its author, a possible scan of an identity document, a machine readable zone in a PDF's text); line and column are 1 unless a text dump says where its rows start, and masked holds the table and columns, or the masked author or position, or the word in the file name. record: a record or file whose structure says it holds special-category data about a person (an HL7 patient segment, a FHIR resource about a patient, a VCF or genotype file, a biometric template); masked then describes the record, never a value.

special_category.description: The GDPR Art. 9 category, or criminal-convictions-and-offences for GDPR Art. 10, for kinds field and record, for kind sink when the data is special-category data, and for kind value when the value is a code that reveals one, such as a diagnosis code.

sink.description: Where the call sends the data, for kind sink.

data_category.description: The kind of personal data, for kind field and for kind sink when a field name says which. Left out for a whole request body or a user-like object.

detector.description: Detector name, as listed by `ato detectors`.

country.description: ISO country code, or EU for identifiers used across countries.

path.description: Path relative to the scanned folder, with forward slashes. Inside an archive or image, `!/` separates the archive from the path within it, as in dump.tar.gz!/data/users.csv or image.tar!/<layer>/etc/app/config.yml.

column_name.description: The data column the value was found in: a CSV or TSV header (#N when the file has no header), a JSON Lines key path such as customer.cnp, or a SQL column. Absent for text without columns.

sample.description: The value is a published example, such as a documentation IBAN or a test card.

fingerprint.description: Stable ID derived from the detector, path and the line with values replaced; never from the value.

possible.description: Other identifiers the value is just as valid for, when nothing near it says which it is; the report then calls it 'Possibly <label> or <label>'.

store.description: The data store, for kind infra.

type.description: Terraform resource type, such as aws_s3_bucket.

name.description: The resource's name in the code.

service.description: Kind of store, such as database, object-storage, queue or log.

regions.description: Regions read from the code; empty when they cannot be read.

personal_data.description: Linked to personal data by a classification tag or a matching table or model name.

not_read.description: The file may hold personal data and was not read in full; it makes the scan exit 3 unless allow_partial is set.
